This report presents the findings of a Tree Risk Assessment and Management Plan prepared by Anderson Environment & Planning (AEP) for the Eastern Cottonwood (Populus deltoides) trees located at John Tucker Park, Paterson.

RESOLUTION 34/2026
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
Councillor Liam Ley
That Council:
  1. Receive and note the Tree Risk Assessment & Management Plan for John Tucker Park, Paterson (AEP Ref: 5890, December 2025).
  2. Approve the removal of 24 trees identified as structurally poor and hazardous and the pruning of 25 trees requiring hazard mitigation.
  3. Undertake a community information meeting prior to any works being undertaken to provide an overview of the approved tree removal and pruning works.
  4. Undertake community consultation on the future management and replacement of the Tucker Park trees and subject to the outcomes, implement a 5–7 year cyclical pruning program for retained Poplars and a staged 10–15 year tree replacement program with improved species diversity and spacing.
Carried

Council has received a proposal from the Campervan & Motorhome Club of Australia (CMCA) to establish a Recreational Vehicle (RV) Park at Abbots Flat Reserve for use by self-contained recreational vehicles.

RESOLUTION 35/2026
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor Fred Paton
That Council:

  1. Note the proposal received from the Campervan & Motorhome Club of Australia Limited (CMCA) regarding the potential establishment of a Recreational Vehicle (RV) Park at Abbots Flat Reserve.

  2. Proceed with negotiations with CMCA regarding the proposed establishment of an RV Park at Abbots Flat Reserve.

  3. Note the proposed layout as the preferred configuration for further feasibility assessment.

  4. Undertake further investigation into infrastructure servicing requirements, including potable water supply and wastewater servicing options such as a pump-out dump point or connection to sewer infrastructure.

  5. Acknowledge potential impacts on existing grazing operations, including relocation of the water trough and removal of existing stockyards.

  6. Following confirmation of the RV development footprint, redefine the remaining grazing land and undertake a market assessment to determine the appropriate lease value or alternate use of the land.

  7. Receive a further report at the next Strategic Property Advisory Committee meeting outlining feasibility findings, proposed lease arrangements and recommended next steps.

  8. Receive a further report to Council prior to entering into any binding agreement with the proponent.

Carried

RESOLUTION 46/2026

Councillor James Campbell

  1. Include the following matters within the scope of the Cemetery Policy Review:

None

Kate Washington MP, and Duty Member for Upper Hunter, Emily Suvaal as the state members of electorates which include the Williams River, seeking support for the establishment of a single agency for river health.
Carried

The report seeks Council adoption of the final Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan following public exhibition and extensive community and agency engagement. The final strategies have been refined to address community feedback and State agency requirements, providing a balanced approach to growth that aligns with the directions and growth expectations of the Hunter Regional Plan 2041.

RESOLUTION 2026/30 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council:
 Note the engagement outcomes of the public exhibition of the Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan as detailed in the Community Visioning and Public Exhibition Engagement Outcomes Report.
  1. Adopt the updated Dungog Shire Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan, which includes the following documents:
    1. Dungog Shire Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan - Executive Summary and Delivery Plan
    2. Dungog Shire Rural Lands Strategy
    3. Dungog Shire Local Housing Strategy
    4. Dungog Structure Plan
    5. Local Strategic Planning Statement - a Growth Management Strategy for Dungog Shire
    6. Dungog Shire Infrastructure Capacity and Prioritisation
  2. Write to those individuals, groups and agencies who took the time to lodge a formal submission to thank them for their input and to advise of Council’s decision. 
  3. Write to DPHI to share a final copy of the Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan and invite their endorsement and acknowledgment of the strategies, along with lodging the revised Local Strategic Planning Statement on the Planning Portal. 
  4. Delegate authority to the General Manager to make minor editorial, formatting and administrative amendments to the final documents where required. Including but not limited to the following:
    1. Revise Investigation Area 2 within Figure 8 of the Dungog Structure Plan mapping to remove existing development not intended to change under the Strategies 
    2. Amend Action 5.9 of the Dungog Shire and Infrastructure Master Plan to acknowledge that further engagement is to be undertaken with the community and relevant agencies regarding the proposed repeal of Clause 4.2A of the Dungog Local Environmental Plan, including consideration of retaining the clause within 5\u202Fkm of urban centres, at the Scoping Report stage of any proposed Local Environmental Plan amendment planning proposal.
    3. Amend Action 12.1 of the Dungog Shire Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan to acknowledge that completion of an Environmental Lands Study or Biodiversity Study (subject to funding) would support appropriate development outcomes or rezoning decisions.
  1. Council staff prepare a project plan outlining post Housing and Infrastructure Master Plan adoption actions required to deliver a comprehensive update to the Local Environmental Plan, Development Control Plan and Contributions Plan, for Council consideration and approval.
  2. Council staff to prepare a detailed brief for an Environmental Lands Study to support applications for grant funding or consideration through Council’s budget process.
Carried

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Ley attended Parliament House with the General Manager and Hunter JO to meet with the Shadow Cabinet, ahead of an election in 12 months. 
On behalf of Dungog Shire, he raised three key issues:
1. Funding Alignment for Planning The current reliance on grants makes long-term planning nearly impossible. Dungog Shire needs a consistent, predictable funding model — it's difficult to commit to a ten-year plan without knowing what funding will be available.
2. Disaster & Betterment Funding The current disaster funding approach is too reactive. A key example was bridge repair funding — when grants were released to multiple councils simultaneously, contractor demand spiked and costs doubled, resulting in a poor use of public money. Liam called for smarter distribution of funds and better timing when allocating money to councils.
3. Road Reclassification Dungog Shire is the only council without a single state-funded road, and Liam argued this needs to change. The current funding model is population-based, which disadvantages small shires. A road connecting Dungog Shire to Maitland receives full funding on the Maitland side but half the funding on Dungog's side — despite being the same road, with the same usage and the same maintenance requirements. ","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Precis
The report presents the results of the recent public exhibition of the Draft Clarence Town Flood Study, provides responses to the public and agency submissions received and recommends the formal adoption of the study by Council. 

RESOLUTION 2026/34 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor Steve Low
That Council:
  1. Note the four (4) written submissions received during the public exhibition period.
  2. Adopt the Clarence Town Flood study and associated mapping compendium in Attachments 5 and 6.
  3. Endorse the update of adopted study and mapping materials within Council’s GIS system. 
  4. Note that, for practical planning purposes, Council staff assess development applications having regard to the Flood Planning Area (FPA), which is based on the 1% Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) 2100 flood level plus 0.5 metres freeboard, and the Probable Maximum Flood (PMF), where relevant.
  5. Note that the General Manager will make arrangements for the provision of educational information to the community to explain flood planning considerations and to assist in allaying community concerns regarding the assessment of flooding impacts in development applications.

In Favour:


Against:		Councillor James Campbell, Councillor Alexandria Carruthers, Councillor Michael Dowling, Councillor Liam Ley, Councillor Fred Paton, Mayor Digby Rayward, Councillor Steve Low
None
Carried 7/0

I, Councillor Alexandria Carruthers, give notice that at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council to be held on 15 April 2026, I intend to move the following motion:

RESOLUTION 2026/51 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
Councillor James Campbell
That Council:
  1. Acknowledges community advocacy, including from the Paterson Progress Association, for improved accessibility at Paterson Train Station.
  2. Notes that Paterson Train Station is a NSW Government asset managed by Transport for NSW, and that accessibility upgrades are the responsibility of the State Government.
  3. Recognises that Paterson Train Station is the most practical and accessible station in the local area due to its central location, existing footpath connections, sealed car parking and all-weather access, in contrast to nearby stations where accessibility infrastructure is limited in usability.
  4. Writes to the local member for Upper Hunter. Dave Layzell MP, Duty Member for Upper Hunter, Emily Suvaal MLC, NSW Minister for Regional Transport the Hon. Jenny Aitchison MP, Transport for NSW, and relevant Federal representatives, including the Federal member for Lyne, Alison Penfold MP, and Duty Senator for Lyne, Deborah O’Neill advocating for the prioritisation and funding of a compliant accessible ramp at Paterson Train Station.
  5. Confirms Council’s role is to advocate on behalf of the community and support local stakeholders in seeking improved accessibility outcomes
Carried

An application has been lodged to modify development consent DA72/2019 for a 30 Lot Subdivision at No 231 Glen William Road, Clarence Town, under S4.55(1A) of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979.  The modification application seeks to amend a condition of consent, which requires bus bays to be constructed along either side of Glen Wiliam Road as part of the subdivision approval. The application to modify the development consent is reported to Council for determination as the requirement for bus bays was specifically added to the recommendation to approve the original development application at the Ordinary Meeting of Council on 15 July 2020.

RESOLUTION 2026/39 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor Steve Low
That Council, as the consent authority pursuant to Clause 4.55(1A) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, modify condition 34 of development consent DA72/2019 as follows:

Stage 2 - The developer shall arrange for detailed engineering design plans to be submitted to Council for approval for: - 

Construction of Road 1 and Road 2 for the full frontage of the Stage 2 lots with associated storm water systems. Plans shall include (but not limited to) the following:
 
  • Construction of the intersection of Road 2 and Glen William Road to a minimum BAR/BAL standard.
  • Construction of a bus bay on either side of Glen William Road.
  • Construction of Road 1 and Road 2 to a Rural Local 2 (RL2) standard.
  • All table drains shall be suitably armored to prevent damage due to scour.
  • Temporary turning heads shall be provided at each termination of Road 1.
All works shall be designed and constructed in accordance with Council’s current Auspec design and construction specification and Council’s Roads Management Strategy.
Advice: All works to be constructed and approved by Council prior to the release of the Subdivision Certificate.

In Favour:


Against:		Councillor James Campbell, Councillor Alexandria Carruthers, Councillor Michael Dowling, Councillor Liam Ley, Councillor Fred Paton, Mayor Digby Rayward, Councillor Steve Low

As part of the Integrated Planning and Reporting (IP&R) requirements under section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act), Council is required to adopt an Operational Plan before the commencement of each financial year. The Operational Plan details the activities Council will undertake as part of the Delivery Program for that year and must include a budget and statement of revenue policy - incorporating proposed rates, fees and charges for the financial year.
The draft Operational Plan 2026-2027 including the Budget and Fees & Charges have been prepared in accordance with IP&R requirements under section 405 of the Act.
Council may now consider placing the documents on public exhibition for 28 days.

RESOLUTION 2026/46 
Moved:
Seconded:		Mayor Digby Rayward
Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
That Council:
  1. Place the Draft Operational Plan 2026-2027, Budget and Fees & Charges on public exhibition for 28 days; and 
  2. Receive a further report following public exhibition to consider any submissions received prior to adopting the Operational Plan 2026-2027, Budget and Fees & Charges.
  3. Waive the Pre‑Development Application Lodgement Meeting and Pre‑Scoping Meeting fees applicable to Development Applications and Planning Proposals, currently $300 as set out in Council’s adopted Fees and Charges, for a period of 12 months, to encourage early consultation with Council staff regarding application requirements.
  4. Undertake community consultation sessions during public exhibition as resources permit and have printed copies available 
Carried

RESOLUTION 2026/37

Carried

A request has been received for Council to consider proposed road/street names for the new road that is being constructed as part of a large lot residential subdivision at 94 Cory Street, Martins Creek.  The request is being reported to Council in accordance with Council’s Street Naming Policy No C3:25.

RESOLUTION 2026/63 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor James Campbell
That Council:
  1. Endorse the two (2) options for consideration by the Geographical Names Board, as follows:
  1. Gostwyck Crescent
  2. Beirnfels Crescent
  1. Submit each of the proposed names in order of preference to the NSW Place and Road Naming Proposal System for approval by the Geographical Names Board.
  1. Following concurrence from the Geographical Names Board, advertise the preferred road name on Council’s website for a period of 28 days for public comment.
  1. Adopt the new street/road names, if no objections are received, and publish notice of the new name in the Government Gazette, and on Council’s website and advise the following relevant parties, through the NSW Place and Road Naming Proposal System:
  1. Australia Post,
  2. the Registrar-General,
  3. the Surveyor-General,
  4. the chief executive of the Ambulance Service of NSW,
  5. Fire and Rescue NSW,
  6. the NSW Rural Fire Service,
  7. the NSW Police Force,
  8. the NSW State Emergency Service,
  9. the NSW Volunteer Rescue Association
  1. In the event objections are received and those objections cannot be satisfied, the matter be reported back to Council for consideration.
Carried

A request has been received for Council to consider proposed road/street names for the new roads that are being constructed as part of a large lot residential subdivision at 231 Glen William Road, Clarence Town.  The request is being reported to Council in accordance with Council’s Street Naming Policy No C3:25.
RESOLUTION 2026/65 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor James Campbell
Councillor Liam Ley
That Council:
  1. Endorse the six (6) road naming options for consideration by the Geographical Names Board, as follows:
    Road 1:
  1. Windmill Way 
  2. Evergreen Drive 
  3. Homestead Drive  
     Road 2: 
  1. Wildflower Close 
  2. Saddlers Close
  3. Valley Close 
  1. Submit each of the proposed names in order of preference to the NSW Place and Road Naming Proposal System for approval by the Geographical Names Board.
  1.  Following concurrence from the Geographical Names Board, advertise the preferred road name on Council’s website for a period of 28 days for public comment.
  1. Adopt the new street/road names, if no objections are received, and publish notice of the new name in the Government Gazette, and on Council’s website and advise the following relevant parties, through the NSW Place and Road Naming Proposal System:
  1. Australia Post,
  2. the Registrar-General,
  3. the Surveyor-General,
  4. the chief executive of the Ambulance Service of NSW,
  5. Fire and Rescue NSW,
  6. the NSW Rural Fire Service,
  7. the NSW Police Force,
  8. the NSW State Emergency Service,
  9. the NSW Volunteer Rescue Association

  1. In the event objections are received and those objections cannot be satisfied, the matter be reported back to Council for consideration.
Carried

- Online Meeting with Ms Steph Cooke, MP - Shadow Minister for Water - Regarding the impact that Hunter Water has on the shire, Development Applications with Hunter Water, also other topics where she may be able to come in and assist us.

This report seeks Council endorsement of the Access and Inclusion Committee Terms of Reference and approval to commence an Expression of Interest (EOI) process for the appointment of community and organisation representatives to the Committee.

RESOLUTION 2026/80 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor James Campbell
That Council:
  1. Endorse the Access and Inclusion Committee Terms of Reference
  2. Endorse the advertising of an Expression of Interest process for community and organisation representatives to join the Access and Inclusion Committee
  3. Note that appointments to the Committee will be undertaken in accordance with the adopted Terms of Reference
  4. Receive a further report detailing recommended appointments following the Expression of Interest process
  5. Note that the Committee will be dissolved upon adoption of the Disability Inclusion Action Plan unless otherwise determined by Council.
Carried 7/0/0

Following the public exhibition of the Operational Plan and Budget 2026-2027 and Fees & Charges 2026-2027, Council may now consider adopting the documents prior to 30 June in accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the NSW Government's Integrated Planning and Reporting Framework.

RESOLUTION 2026/87 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
That Council: 
  1. Receive and note the 25 community submissions received during the public exhibition period;
  2. Note the changes made to the draft documents following public exhibition and consideration of submissions, as outlined in this report;
  3. Adopt the Operational Plan and Budget 2026-2027 and Fees & Charges 2026-2027;
  4. Approve expenditure and vote money as detailed within the Council Budget 2026-2027;
  5. Write to those members of the community, business and organisations who took the time to lodge a public submission to thank them for their input and advise of Council's decision; and 
  6. The General Manager be delegated authority to make amendments of a minor nature to the format or layout of the final documents if required.
  7. Endorse the 28 day public exhibition of the proposed Category B(a) Planning Proposal Fee and that a further report be presented to the Council to consider any submissions made during the public exhibition period prior to adoption, and that if no submissions are made the fees be adopted on completion of public exhibition.
  8. That action 4.3.2.3 on page 119 and 120 be subject to a report to be brought back to Council in August 2026.
Carried 7/0/0

Council is required to make the rates and charges for the financial year commencing 1 July 2026 in accordance with Sections 535, 537 & 538 of the Local Government Act 1993

RESOLUTION 2026/88 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
Councillor Liam Ley

That in accordance with Chapter 15 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make the following rates and charges for the year 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027:

  1. ORDINARY RATES

    1. The Farmland Category of the Ordinary Rate shall consist of a Base Amount to which an ad valorem amount is added, as follows:
      1. the Base Amount shall be six hundred and sixty three dollars and ten cents ($663.10) on all rateable land within the category, within the Shire; and
        the percentage of the total amount payable by the levying of the Rate for the Farmland Category of the Ordinary Rate that the levying of the Base Amount will produce, is 14.9%.
      2. the ad valorem amount shall be zero point two one nine nine (0.2199) cents in the dollar applied to the land value of all rateable land within the category, within the Shire.

    2. The Residential Category, excepting Sub-categories Clarence Town, Dungog and Village, of the Ordinary Rate shall consist of a Base Amount to which an ad valorem amount is added, as follows:
      1. the Base Amount shall be six hundred and seventy-five dollars and ninety-five cents ($675.95) on all rateable land within the category, within the Shire; and
        the percentage of the total amount payable by the levying of the Rate for the Residential Category of the Ordinary Rate that the levying of the Base Amount will produce, is 32.1%.
      2. the ad valorem amount shall be zero point two zero three one (0.2031) cents in the dollar applied to the land value of all rateable land within the category, within the Shire. 
    3. The Residential - Clarence Town Sub-category of the Ordinary Rate shall consist of a Base Amount to which an ad valorem amount is added, as follows:
      1. the Base Amount shall be five hundred and twenty-nine dollars and zero cents ($529.00) on all rateable land within the sub-category, within the Shire; and
        the percentage of the total amount payable by the levying of the Rate for the Residential - Clarence Town Sub-category of the Ordinary Rate that the levying of the Base Amount will produce, is 37.6%.
      2. the ad valorem amount shall be zero point two four one two (0.2412) cents in the dollar applied to the land value of all rateable land within the sub-category, within the Shire.

Council has received a proposal to name the playing field at Vacy Sportsground as "Keith & Lesley Miles Oval" in recognition of the significant contribution made by the late Keith and Lesley Miles to the Vacy community and local sport.

RESOLUTION 2026/82 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council:
  1. Note the written support provided by the Vacy Sportsground Section 355 Committee for the proposed naming of the playing field at Vacy Sportsground as Keith & Lesley Miles Oval (Attachment 1)
  2. Acknowledge the significant contribution made by the late Keith and Lesley Miles to the Vacy community and local sporting organisations.
  3. In the absence of a Council Reserve Naming Policy, endorse commencement of the formal process to consider naming the playing field at Vacy Sportsground as Keith & Lesley Miles Oval.
  4. Place the proposal on public exhibition for a period of 28 days.
  5. Invite submissions from sporting clubs, user groups, community organisations and the broader community.
  6. Receive a further report following completion of the consultation process.
Carried 7/0/0

Following the passing of a disallowance motion against the Local Government (General) Amendment (Model Code of Meeting Practice) Regulation 2025 in the NSW Legislative Council on 26 May 2026, Council must rescind the Dungog Shire Council Code of Meeting Practice 2026 adopted by Council at its meeting of 10 December 2025.

RESOLUTION 2026/77 
Moved:
Seconded:		Mayor Digby Rayward
None
That Council:
  1. Rescind Resolution 2025/123 adopted by Council on 10 December 2026 which effectively rescinds the 2025 Dungog Shire Council Code of Meeting Practice; and 
  2. Note that rescinding the 2025 Dungog Shire Council Code of Meeting Practice adopted on 10 December 2026, will have the effect of reinstating the previous Code of Meeting Practice adopted by Council at its meeting of 16 July 2025. 
  3. Prepare a new draft Code of Meeting Practice for public exhibition which will also include the supplementary provisions relating to identifying the expenditure of funds for notices of motion or mayoral minutes that recommend actions that would result in expenditure of funds outside of the adopted Council Operational Plan and Budget.

RESOLUTION 2026/83 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council:

  2. Accept the advance funding payment of $2,628,387.94 from the NSW Reconstruction Authority to support delivery of the approved AGRN 1170 restoration works.

  4. Note that the advance funding must only be expended on restoration works approved as eligible Essential Public Asset Restoration projects under the NSW Essential Public Assets Restoration Natural Disaster Grant Program.
  5. Note that Council will develop a project delivery plan, including milestone-based payment schedules, to support delivery of the approved works and management of project cashflow.
  6. Receive a further report detailing the approved works program, project delivery schedule and procurement arrangements through either an Ordinary Council Meeting or the Quarterly Budget Review process.
Carried 7/0/0

This report provides an update on the public exhibition of the proposed naming of the playing field at Vacy Sportsground and seeks Council's endorsement of the preferred name, subject to the outcome of the exhibition.

RESOLUTION 2026/111 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor James Campbell
That Council:
  1. Note the proposal to name the playing field at Vacy Sportsground as Keith & Lesley Miles Oval was placed on public exhibition from 19 June 2026 to 17 July 2026.
  2. Note that, as at the preparation of this report, no formal submissions have been received.
  3. Subject to no formal submissions being received opposing the proposed naming by 19 July 2026, endorse the naming of the playing field at Vacy Sportsground as Keith & Lesley Miles Oval.
  4. Should a formal submission be received by 19 July 2026 that does not support the proposed naming, receive a further report prior to determining whether the proposed naming should proceed.
  5. Authorise the General Manager to complete all administrative actions associated with the naming should no formal submissions be received by 19 July 2026.
  6. Note that the official naming and unveiling ceremony will be held on 15 August 2026 at Vacy Sportsground in conjunction with the Paterson River Rugby League Club's final home game of the 2026 season and Old Boys Day.
Carried 6/0/0

This report responds to the Notice of Motion requesting an assessment of potential locations for additional 24-hour caravan and RV parking across the Dungog Local Government Area and provides recommendations regarding site suitability and implementation.

RESOLUTION 2026/112 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council:
  1. Receive and note the report regarding potential locations for additional 24-hour caravan and recreational vehicle (RV) parking within the Dungog Local Government Area.
  2. Note that Frank Robinson Reserve remains Council's existing designated 24-hour RV parking location.
  3. Note that Abbotts Flat Reserve is currently the subject of ongoing investigations with the third-party provider regarding the development of a dedicated RV Park and has therefore not been considered further as part of this assessment.
  4. Note that Bandon Grove Park and Vacy Memorial Green are considered the most suitable locations for future implementation, subject to detailed assessment, funding and any required approvals.
  5. Note that camping within Council parks and reserves would generally require planning approval and/or amendments to the relevant Plan of Management and is therefore not recommended as an immediate implementation option.
  6. Consider funding for any future implementation of additional 24-hour caravan and RV parking locations through the annual budget process and available grant funding.
Carried 6/0/0

  3. Note that Abbotts Flat Reserve is currently the subject of ongoing investigations with the third-party provider regarding the development of a dedicated RV Park and has therefore not been considered further as part of this assessment.
  4. Note that Bandon Grove Park and Vacy Memorial Green are considered the most suitable locations for future implementation, subject to detailed assessment, funding and any required approvals.
  5. Note that camping within Council parks and reserves would generally require planning approval and/or amendments to the relevant Plan of Management and is therefore not recommended as an immediate implementation option.
  6. Consider funding for any future implementation of additional 24-hour caravan and RV parking locations through the annual budget process and available grant funding.

Precis

This matter is referred to Council for determination under the Assessment of Development Application Policy and the Code of Conduct (pecuniary interest) on the basis that the applicant and landowner is a relative of a Council employee.

Development Application No. 210/2025 for a one into two lot subdivision of 139 Mulconda Lane, Bandon Grove was approved under delegated authority by Council on 24 December 2025.

Sections of Mulconda Lane are physically located outside Council’s legally identified road reserve (i.e. parts of the actual road run across private property). In accordance with Council’s Managing Road Encroachments Policy a condition was imposed requiring the dedication of that private land which contains the road across to Council. This application seeks to remove this condition under section 4.55(1A) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 (EP&A Act).

The application has been assessed against the requirements of the EP&A Act and is considered satisfactory. It is recommended that the application be approved.


RESOLUTION 2026/103 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Michael Dowling
Councillor Steve Low AM
That Council approve the application to modify Development Approval No. 210/2025 under section 4.55(1A) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.
In Favour:
Councillor James Campbell, Councillor Michael Dowling, Councillor Liam Ley, Councillor Fred Paton, Mayor Digby Rayward, Councillor Steve Low AM

None
Abstain:None
Carried 6/0/0

This report seeks to rescind Point 3 of Resolution 2026/77 adopted by Council at the Ordinary Meeting of 17 June 2026 relating to the exhibition of a new Code of Meeting Practice. The Office of Local Government advised on 25 June 2026, that under Section 8 of the Subordinate Legislation Act 1989, Councils cannot adopt a new code within four months of a parliamentary disallowance. Additionally, internal review indicates that the newly reinstated 16 July 2025 Code already includes Council's desired financial oversight provisions. In this regard, a new public exhibition is legally restricted and unnecessary.

RESOLUTION 2026/116 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council 
  1. Rescind point 3 of Resolution 2026/77 adopted at Council's meeting of 17 June 2026 which stated:
3. Prepare a new draft Code of Meeting Practice for public exhibition which will also include the supplementary provisions relating to identifying the expenditure of funds for notices of motion or mayoral minutes that recommend actions that would result in expenditure of funds outside of the adopted Council Operational Plan and Budget.

  1. Note that this rescission is required because the Subordinate Legislation Act 1989 and making of the Local Government (General) Amendment (Meetings) Regulation 2026 (2026 Regulation) on 26 June 2026, prevents the timely prescription of a new Code of Meeting Practice following a parliamentary disallowance, and because the reinstated 16 July 2025 Code of Meeting Practice already contains adequate financial implication frameworks.
  1. Delegate authority to the General Manager to format and strike out Clauses 3.32 to 3.37 of the reinstated Dungog Shire Council Code of Meeting Practice (adopted 16 July 2025) to clarify to the community that past pre-meeting briefing provisions are voided by the overriding 2026 Regulation.
  1. Note the revised pre-meeting briefing requirements under the 2026 Regulation, which permit only the Mayor or Committee Chairpersons to meet with executive staff regarding upcoming agendas, while requiring Councillor questions regarding the Agenda to be made in writing and published on the website where practicable unless they relate to a confidential matter under section 10A of the Local Government Act 1993.
Carried 6/0/0

Following the Independent Grants Management Review by a consultant last year, Council adopted a Grants Management Strategy at its meeting of 18 February 2026.

At the same meeting Council adopted the draft Grants Management Policy for public exhibition. 
No submissions were received during the public exhibition period of 19 February to 19 March 2026.   Minor edits are proposed to improve wording and align with the recent organisation structure change without changing Council's strategic intent, as shown in the attached track-changes version of the Policy.

The Policy provides the formal governance framework to support implementation of the Grants Management Strategy and addresses corporate risks identified in the Review. The Policy sets Council's requirements, delegations, and accountabilities for all grant activities to optimise external funding from grant opportunities. 

RESOLUTION 2026/121 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Michael Dowling
Councillor Liam Ley

To provide Council with an update on the delivery of the $25 Million Special Purpose Grant Program and seek endorsement of proposed amendments to the approved works program.

RESOLUTION 2026/144 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Michael Dowling
Councillor Steve Low AM
That Council:
  1. Receive and note the report.
  2. Endorse the revised $25 Million Special Purpose Grant Program as outlined within this report.
  3. Endorse the reallocation of funding within the Program to facilitate completion of the Cory Street, Martins Creek and King Street, Paterson rehabilitation projects.
  4. Endorse the removal of the following projects from the current $25 Million Special Purpose Grant Program:
      • Main Street, Paterson
      • Verge Street, Dungog
      • Baird Street, Dungog
      • Hospital Road, Dungog
      • Myles Street, Dungog
  5. Note that the above projects remain priority road rehabilitation projects and will continue to be delivered through Council's forward Capital Works Program utilising alternative funding sources as funding becomes available.
  6. Note that the Paterson River Road rehabilitation project, previously removed from the Special Purpose Grant Program by Council resolution in February 2024, has subsequently been incorporated into Council's forward Capital Works Program, with staged delivery proposed during the 2026/27 and 2027/28 financial years.
  7. Note the approved extension of the Transport for NSW Funding Agreement until 30 June 2027.
Carried 7/0/0

Precis
To update Council on the implementation of the proposed Plans of Management and Master Plans Forward Schedule 2026–2029, advise of the financial implications identified through the quotation process and seek endorsement of the staged delivery schedule.

Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor James Campbell
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council:
  1. Endorse the Plans of Management and Master Plans Forward Schedule 2026–2029.
  2. Note the financial implications associated with implementing the priority projects identified within the Forward Schedule.
  3. Note that the quotations received indicate that delivery of the Forward Schedule will require a greater level of investment than originally anticipated.
  4. Note that the John Tucker Park Plan of Management and Master Plan and the Swimming Pool Master Plan and Business Plan can proceed as they have existing funding allocations through Section 7.11 contributions and adopted budgets.
  5. Receive a further report outlining alternative delivery models, resource requirements and funding options for the remaining Plans of Management and Master Plan projects.
  6. Support continued engagement with Crown Lands NSW to better understand the status of unresolved Aboriginal Land Claims affecting Crown land managed by Council and, where appropriate, seek priority assessment of claims where significant Council investment is proposed.
Carried 7/0/0

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Precis
This report outlines the investigation into extending the operating season of the Dungog Memorial and Clarence Town Swimming Pools and presents the findings and options for Council's consideration.

MOTION 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor James Campbell
Councillor Liam Ley
That Council:
    1. Note the findings of the investigation into extending the operating season of the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool and Clarence Town Swimming Pool.
    2. Note the strong community support for extending the swimming season and Council's ongoing investment in maintaining and improving both facilities.
    3. Note that the investigation has identified significant infrastructure, heating and financial constraints associated with extending the swimming season into September under the current operating arrangements.
    4. Endorse commencement of the 2026–2027 swimming season at the Dungog Memorial and Clarence Town Swimming Pools on Saturday 26 September 2026.
    5. Receive a further report for Council's February 2027 Ordinary Meeting on the feasibility of extending the 2026–2027 swimming season to 30 April 2027, having regard to the operational, financial, infrastructure and patronage outcomes from the 2026–2027 season.
    6. Continue to progress Operational Plan Action 4.3.2.2 – Facility Assessment and Operational Review of the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool and Clarence Town Swimming Pool to inform future service delivery, asset management priorities and funding opportunities.
Lost 2/5/0 

The motion was lost and the original motion was moved.

RESOLUTION 2026/137 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Steve Low AM
Councillor Michael Dowling
That Council:
    1. Note the findings of the investigation into extending the operating season of the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool and Clarence Town Swimming Pool.
    2. Note the strong community support for extending the swimming season and Council's ongoing investment in maintaining and improving both facilities.
    3. Note that the investigation has identified significant infrastructure, heating and financial constraints associated with extending the swimming season into September under the current operating arrangements.
    4. Endorse commencement of the 2026–2027 swimming season at the Dungog Memorial and Clarence Town Swimming Pools on Monday, 28 September 2026.
    5. Receive a further report for Council's February 2027 Ordinary Meeting on the feasibility of extending the 2026–2027 swimming season to 30 April 2027, having regard to the operational, financial, infrastructure and patronage outcomes from the 2026–2027 season.
    6. Continue to progress Operational Plan Action 4.3.2.2 – Facility Assessment and Operational Review of the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool and Clarence Town Swimming Pool to inform future service delivery, asset management priorities and funding opportunities.
Carried 7/0/0

","parentId":1439,"sortOrder":43,"minutesSortOrder":12,"minutesParentId":1439,"outlineNumber":"1.","fullOutlineNumber":"9.1.","htmlContent":"

The opening of the new Clarence Town Bridge marks an important milestone for the community, providing a safe and reliable crossing of the Williams River while allowing the heritage-listed Brig O'Johnston Bridge to be preserved.

The Brig O'Johnston Bridge is one of New South Wales' most significant heritage bridges and is an important part of the history of Clarence Town and the Dungog Shire. Its heritage value is recognised and respected by our community.

However, the reported cost of rehabilitating the bridge has raised a much broader question about the allocation of limited public infrastructure funding. At a time when local Councils across regional New South Wales face unprecedented road maintenance backlogs and deteriorating infrastructure, it is appropriate to ask whether the current Heritage Bridge Conservation Strategy continues to represent the best use of taxpayers' funds.

This is not an argument against heritage. It is an argument for ensuring that public investment delivers the greatest possible benefit to the communities it serves.

RESOLUTION 2026/131 
Moved:
Seconded:		Mayor Digby Rayward
None
That Council:
  1. Request Transport for NSW provide Council with:
    • the verified rehabilitation cost and scope;
    • projected whole-of-life maintenance costs;
    • the business case and cost-benefit analysis;
    • the alternatives considered; and
    • confirmation of whether any savings could be redirected to regional or local roads.
  2. Council Receive a further report once this information is provided, so it can determine its position with the above information at hand
  3. Reaffirm Council’s advocacy for increased, dedicated funding for state, regional and local roads.
Carried 7/0/0

MOTION

Councillor Liam Ley
That Dungog Shire Council:
  1. Thanks all residents and community organisations for their engagement with Council on this matter to date.
  2. Notes the over 300-year-old age of the Hospital Hill Red Gum as estimated by Sustaining the Williams Valley, and shall collaborate with local landcare groups to take proactive measures to cultivate saplings of the tree to be planted elsewhere around Dungog.
  3. Notes the exceptional importance of this Red Gum to the Dungog community as a figure of great historical significance as the old Christmas tree of years gone by, and to the wider ecosystem which the flowers & hollows this tree supports.
  4. Supports Council staff in their ongoing investigation of all costs and options in Council’s design process currently underway for the ‘Hospital Road Dungog - Mackay Street to Scott Avenue’ capital works program.

This report seeks Council endorsement of the Fair Funding 4 Dungog campaign brand and proposed campaign components. The campaign is intended to strengthen Council’s advocacy ahead of the NSW State Election by building community awareness and support for fairer State Government investment in Dungog Shire. 

RESOLUTION 2026/164 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
Councillor James Campbell
That Council:
  1. Approve the Fair Funding 4 Dungog campaign brand, as presented in Attachment 1.
  2. Endorse the proposed campaign methodology outlined in this report to support Council’s advocacy in the lead-up to the NSW State Election.
  3. Note that the campaign will be positive, respectful, evidence-based and politically neutral, with advocacy directed consistently to all relevant political parties and candidates.
  4. Endorse the progressive development and implementation of campaign materials, including a campaign website, social media content, videos, community engagement materials, signage, print advertising, stakeholder communications and advocacy collateral.
  5. Delegate authority to the General Manager to approve minor amendments to campaign messaging, creative applications and implementation activities where required, provided they remain consistent with Council’s adopted Advocacy Strategy and the principles outlined in this report.
Carried 7/0/0

This report seeks Council approval of a new corporate brand for Dungog Shire Council, developed in consultation with Councillors and Council’s Executive Leadership Team to provide a contemporary, professional and distinctive identity that reflects the organisation’s future direction while retaining a strong connection to the unique character of the Dungog Shire.

RESOLUTION 2026/161 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
Councillor James Campbell
That Council:
  1. Approve the new Dungog Shire Council corporate brand, as presented in Attachment 1.
  2. Endorse the gradual implementation of the new corporate brand across Council’s communications, digital platforms, publications, signage, uniforms, vehicles and other corporate materials.
  3. Note that implementation will be undertaken progressively across existing materials, and assets replaced or updated as appropriate to minimise unplanned budget allocations.
  4. Hold a community information session to inform the community on how the brand was created and the rationale of the typography, icon, colours and applications.
  5. Note that this is a corporate brand and the destination and tourism brand sits separate in partnership with Dungog Regional Tourism and stakeholders.
Carried 7/0/0

I welcome the NSW Local Government Grants Commission's acknowledgement that current Financial Assistance Grants arrangements limit the full application of Horizontal Fiscal Equalisation, reinforcing Council's long-standing advocacy for fairer funding outcomes. I recommend that Council continue to pursue reforms that better support fair funding for Dungog Shire.

RESOLUTION 2026/160 
Moved:
Seconded:		Mayor Digby Rayward
None
That Council:
  1. Receive and note the Mayoral Minute.
  2. Note the correspondence from the Chair of the NSW Local Government Grants Commission which acknowledges that the National Principles governing Financial Assistance Grants inhibit the full application of Horizontal Fiscal Equalisation in the distribution of grant funding. 
  3. Reaffirm Council's long-standing advocacy for:
    • restoration of Financial Assistance Grants to 1% of Commonwealth taxation revenue;
    • reform of the Commonwealth Financial Assistance Grants framework to better achieve Horizontal Fiscal Equalisation outcomes;
    • sustainable funding arrangements for rural and regional local government.
  4. Write to:
    • The Hon Catherine King MP, Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government;
    • The Hon Kristy McBain MP, Minister for Regional Development, Local Government and Territories;
    • Ms Alison Penfold MP, Member for Lyne;
    • Mr Dave Layzell MP, Member for Upper Hunter;
    • The Hon Jenny Aitchison MP, Minister for Roads;
    • Cr Darcy Byrne, President of Local Government NSW; and
    • Cr Matt Burnett, President of the Australian Local Government Association; and
    • Senator Deborah O'Neill, Duty Member for Lyne
    • MLC Emily Suvaal, Duty Member for Upper Hunter
advising them of Council's position and seeking support for reforms to the Federal Local Government (Financial Assistance) Act and the NSW Local Government Grants Commission methodology to enable the fuller application of Horizontal Fiscal Equalisation principles in the distribution of Financial Assistance Grants.
  1. Participate in the NSW Local Government Grants Commission review process and make submissions supporting a methodology that directs funding to councils with the greatest relative need consistent with Horizontal Fiscal Equalisation principles.
Carried 7/0/0

Cr Campbell provided a report on the Dungog Youth Council. 
On Monday, I participated in Dungog Youth Council’s most recent meeting in which they held a workshop with Dungog’s own Matthew Coxhill.

The workshop focussed on how to facilitate a well run event - an invaluable skill being passed onto an active and keen group of emerging young leaders in our community.

The Dungog Youth Council has been active for well over 9 months now and have held many fundraisers, and a camp up at Wangat Lodge. And the ongoing efforts of the Youth Council team is well worth recognising and encouraging where possible as the leadership and values of the not so distant future of our Shire.

Well done to Claire and the whole team!

This report presents the evaluation of tenders received for Tender T02/2026 for the design and construction of permanent remediation works at the Flat Tops Road and Monkerai Road landslips. 

RESOLUTION 2026/190 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor Liam Ley
That Council:
  1. Decline to accept all tenders received for Tender T02/2026 - AGRN 1025 Landslips - Flat Tops Road and Monkerai Road, in accordance with clause 178(1)(b) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021.
  2. Resolve, pursuant to clause 178(3)(e) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, to enter into a negotiation process with all three tenderers that submitted tenders under T02/2026, with a view to entering into a contract in relation to the subject matter of the tender.
  3. Note that fresh tenders are not proposed because the market has recently been tested through an open tender process, three suitably experienced tenderers have submitted proposals, the underlying project remains the same and repeating the open tender process is unlikely to provide a material benefit relative to the additional cost and delay.
  4. Authorise the General Manager to conduct negotiations with the three tenderers.
  5. Delegate authority to the General Manager to accept the most advantageous negotiated offer and enter into a contract without a further report to Council, provided that the negotiated contract price, together with all remaining forecast project costs and appropriate contingency, does not exceed the available approved project funding.
  6. Authorise the General Manager to execute all necessary contract documents.
  7. Require a further report to Council if the conditions above cannot be satisfied, including where the negotiated outcome exceeds the available project funding or involves a material change to the scope.
Carried 7/0/0

Development Application No. 241/2025 seeks consent for an intensive livestock agriculture operation comprising of a small scale rotational outdoor piggery (pig farm) at 3565 Allyn River Road, Upper Allyn. In accordance with the provisions of Council’s Assessment of Development Applications Policy, the application is reported to Council for determination as, in the opinion of the Director of Planning and Environment, the development application is significant and/or of community interest and as such Council’s consideration of the development application is required.

RESOLUTION 2026/171 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Fred Paton
Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
That Council:
  1. Defer the matter to allow the applicant more time to address the report’s concerns through an agronomist or other independent technical specialist, at the applicant’s expense;
  2. That subject to the concerns being satisfactorily addressed, a further report with draft conditions of consent be provided to Council for consideration; and
  3. Conduct a site visit prior to the report coming back to Council.

In Favour:
Councillor Alexandria Carruthers, Councillor Michael Dowling, Councillor Liam Ley, Councillor Fred Paton, Mayor Digby Rayward, Councillor Steve Low AM
Against:
None
Abstain:Councillor James Campbell
Carried 6/0/1

To update Council on the revised delivery approach for priority Plans of Management and Master Plans and seek endorsement of the proposed project scopes and funding required to progress the 2026/27 program.

RESOLUTION 2026/176 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Steve Low AM
Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
That Council:
  1. Receive and note the update on the review of alternative delivery models for the Plans of Management and Master Plans Forward Schedule 2026–2029.
  2. Continue the proposed engagement and delivery of the John Tucker Park Plan of Management and Master Plan and the Swimming Pool Master Plan and Business Plan, consistent with their existing funding allocations and the adopted Forward Schedule.
  3. Place the Pilchers Reserve Plan of Management on hold until further notice, pending consultation with relevant Local Aboriginal Land Councils and advise the Pilchers Reserve Plan of Management Committee accordingly.
  4. Investigate appropriate measures to clarify and further delineate access arrangements to Pilchers Reserve, including communicating the designated access arrangements through information signage at relevant locations, installing route markers from Wallaringa/Hanleys Creek Road to Pilchers Reserve and installing gates where appropriate.
  5. Endorse the preparation of the Dungog Cemeteries Strategic Management Framework primarily through internal Council resources, including relevant policies, operational plans, procedures and supporting management documentation, with external consultants engaged where specialist expertise or technical input is required and collaboration with other councils and relevant agencies undertaken for advice, benchmarking and assistance.
  6. Endorse a revised scope for the Williams River Holiday Park strategic planning project, comprising a Business Plan and Concept Master Plan, focused on improving the management, functionality and serviceability of the site and providing a framework to guide future planning, operations and investment.
  7. Continue engagement with the external consultant for the Unnamed Reserve on Hooke Street Plan of Management to progress preparation of the Plan.
  8. Approve the reprioritisation of $100,000 from within Council’s existing 2026/27 operational budget to fund Council’s contribution towards the identified priority Plans of Management, Master Plans and associated strategic planning projects, with the specific budget adjustments to be identified and reported through the September 2026 Quarterly Budget Review.
Carried 7/0/0

To seek Council endorsement to re-establish the Weeds and Biosecurity Advisory Committee, adopt revised Terms of Reference and call for Expressions of Interest for community representatives.

RESOLUTION 2026/177 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Michael Dowling
Councillor Fred Paton
That Council:
  1. Rescind the current Weeds and Biosecurity Advisory Committee and the existing community member appointments, noting that the current Terms of Reference provide for a two-year term of appointment.
  2. Endorse the revised Terms of Reference for the Dungog Shire Council Weeds and Biosecurity Advisory Committee.

  5. Note that Cr Low is Council’s current appointed Alternate Councillor representative on the Weeds and Biosecurity Advisory Committee.
  6. Note that following completion of the Expression of Interest process, a further report will be presented to Council seeking appointment of community representatives to the Committee.
  7. Thank the outgoing community members for their contribution to the Weeds and Biosecurity Advisory Committee.
Carried 7/0/0

A draft Cyber Security Policy has been developed to establish Council's approach to managing cyber security risks, protecting information and technology assets and strengthening organisational cyber resilience. The policy provides a governance framework to support the secure operation of Council systems and services and aligns with current legislative obligations and contemporary cyber security practices.

RESOLUTION 2026/193 
Moved:
Seconded:		Councillor Liam Ley
Councillor Alexandria Carruthers
That Council:
  1. Adopt the draft Cyber Security Policy
  2. Delegate authority to the General Manager to make minor administrative and formatting changes to the Policy as necessary
  3. Note that public exhibition is not required as the policy relates to internal governance, information security and operational management arrangements and public disclosure of cyber security governance controls may increase security risks to Council
Carried 7/0/0

Dungog Shire Council's "Fair Funding 4 Dungog" advocacy campaign and the Mayoral Facebook video updates regarding funding inequity in the NSW Block Grants have prompted formal acknowledgement from Minister Jenny Aitchison MP regarding regional road funding inequities. 

RESOLUTION 2026/168 
Moved:
Mayor Digby Rayward
That Council:
  1. Welcomes the formal acknowledgement from the Minister for Roads and Minister for regional Transport, the Hon. Jenny Aitchison MP, in response to Council's advocacy calling out systemic inequity in the NSW Block Grants methodology; and
  2. Write to Minister Aitchison:
    1. Thanking her for the response and formal acknowledgement of regional road funding inequity;
    2. Seeking engagement and input to the foreshadowed consideration of future Block Grant Funding models and requesting that this be carried out prior to the NSW State elections in 2027; and
    3. Requesting a formal meeting to further discuss ongoing funding inequity and research currently underway on the true costs to maintain the regional road network in the Dungog Shire.
    4. Advising that Council is currently collecting the required data in order to submit our road recategorisation applications.
Carried 7/0/0

I am pleased to report that the NSW Local Government Grants Commission has invited us to provide feedback on their proposed Financial Assistance Grants methodology review. This review is a major win for our long-standing advocacy and our "Fair Funding 4 Dungog" Campaign, but we must keep the pressure on to guarantee the final model delivers the best possible outcome for Dungog Shire.

RESOLUTION 2026/169 
Moved:
Mayor Digby Rayward
That Council:

  1. Receive and note the correspondence from the Chair of the NSW Local Government Grants Commission dated 4 September 2026.
  2. Welcome the review by the NSW Local Government Grants Commission into the distribution methodology of the Federal Financial Assistance Grants across NSW Councils and acknowledge that Dungog Shire Council has long advocated for such a review to ensure a fairer, needs-based distribution to rural and regional councils.
  3. Prepare a formal submission in consultation with the Mayor and Councillors prior to the presentation closing date of 9 October 2026.
  4. Authorise the Mayor and General Manager to sign and lodge the final submission on behalf of Council.
Carried 7/0/0

This report provides an update on additional epoxy painting works at the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool and arrangements to manage any potential delay to the 28 September 2026 opening.

RESOLUTION 2026/170 
Moved:
Mayor Digby Rayward
That Council:
  1. Note the additional essential epoxy painting works identified at the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool following the August 2026 Council report. 
  2. Note that Council has expedited the works and is working with Hunter Water to investigate options to accelerate filling of the pool. 
  3. Note that Council continues to work towards opening the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool on 28 September 2026, subject to successful filling, water balancing, commissioning and operational readiness. 
  4. Endorse 2 October 2026 as the contingency opening date should the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool not be ready to safely open on 28 September 2026. 
  5. Delegate authority to the General Manager to open the Dungog Memorial Swimming Pool prior to 2 October 2026 once satisfied that all commissioning, water quality, operational and safety requirements have been met. 
  6. Note that the Clarence Town Swimming Pool remains scheduled to open on 28 September 2026. 
Carried 7/0/0

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();
    </script>

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();
    </script>

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();
    </script>
